**Simplified Final Diagnosis Report**

**Main Injury:**
The 18-year-old male suffered a fatal shotgun wound that entered his left arm, traveled through his chest, and exited his right arm.

**Details of the Injury:**
The shotgun slug entered the left arm from the back, went through the arm tissue, and then re-entered the body through the left armpit. It then went through the chest muscle, broke the first rib, and damaged the area between the lungs (mediastinum). The slug also hurt the main artery that carries blood to the lungs and the right side of the heart. It then broke the right first and second ribs, went through the chest muscle, and exited the body through the right arm.

**Other Relevant Information:**
The shotgun slug was found in the victim's clothing. The victim also had fluid in both lungs (hemothoraces). Additionally, the victim had a history of a heart condition (tricuspid atresia and hypoplastic right ventricle) that was treated with a Fontan procedure, but the procedure was still intact.

**Cause of Death:**
The cause of death was the solitary shotgun wound to the chest, and also the patient had cirrhosis and a history of heart conditions.

The final diagnosis was that the 18-year-old male died from a shotgun wound. The wound entered through the back of his left arm, and it damaged the soft tissue. It then moved to the left armpit and went through the chest muscles, breaking the first rib and damaging the space in front of the heart. It also hurt the pulmonary artery, the right atrium, and broke two more ribs on the right side, going through the chest muscles before exiting.

The bullet went from left to right, downwards, and slightly towards the front. The spent shotgun bullet and its packaging were found in the person's clothes. There was also blood in both sides of the chest.

The young man had a previous heart condition, and he had a special surgery called a Fontan procedure. However, this old surgery was not the cause of death. His heart and liver were also examined and found to have some problems, but they were not the cause of death either.

The final diagnosis of the 18-year-old male was a fatal shotgun wound to the chest, and this was the cause of death. The bullet first entered through the left arm, and then it re-entered the body through the left armpit. The bullet damaged the muscles of the chest, broke through the first rib, and went through the chest cavity, also known as the hemithorax, causing significant harm to the pulmonary artery and the right atrium. Additionally, it broke the first and second ribs on the right side and exited the body through the right chest, hitting the inner right arm.

The bullet also caused internal bleeding in both the left and right hemithoraces, which are the spaces between the lungs and the chest wall. Furthermore, it was noted that the individual had a pre-existing medical condition, specifically, a Fontan procedure for a heart defect. And, notably, the Fontan anastomosis remained intact, but the individual had adhesions on the pericardium, which is the sac around the heart, as well as an enlarged right atrium and liver damage.

The young man, 18, died from a single shotgun wound that went through his chest. The bullet entered his left arm and moved through his chest, and also damaged his lungs and heart. It then went through his right chest and exited through his right arm. 

The bullet's path was from left to right, and slightly downward and forward. A spent shotgun slug was found in his clothing. The young man had two collapsed lungs due to bleeding, but also had pre-existing heart issues. He had surgery in the past to correct problems with his heart. 

The surgery, called a Fontan procedure, connected parts of his heart, which were still intact. However, there were also some adhesions, which are abnormal fibrous bands that can form after surgery. His heart was also slightly larger than normal, but his liver was diseased and had a condition called micronodular cirrhosis.
